title: Trident: lightweight session reconstructor, reconnect shim, and rate-aware retry policy (go-sdk v1.4.0)
author: Priya Kaur
release_notes: Go SDK v1.4.0: adds a lightweight session reconstruction helper for streaming clients, introduces a rate-aware retry policy (token-bucket backoff) that better handles 429s when using Dedicated capacity, improves Context propagation in stream iterators, and bumps the module version to v1.4.0.
description:
Motivation: Several customers reported edge cases where long-running streaming sessions would lose the server-side session ID after a transient network partition, causing a hard drop in throughput and noisy error spikes during retries. At the same time, the generic exponential backoff was underperforming against bursty 429s from Dedicated pools: it wasted latency during short-lived throttles and caused token stalls for multi-connection clients.

What this PR does: Adds a small, opt-in session reconstructor (internal name: TridentSession) for Go streaming clients that can attempt a graceful reconnect and rehydrate a lightweight client-side session blob instead of always starting from a fresh handshake. The reconstructor is deliberately minimal: it stores a short-lived session token + stream cursor and exposes two exported helpers: ReconnectWithGrace(ctx, conn) and SnapshotSession() which are intended for higher-level apps that maintain long-lived streams.

In parallel we introduce a rate-aware retry policy (rateaware.Backoff) that pairs an adaptive token-bucket throttler with jittered backoff. For 429/Quota responses the policy tries short, frequent small waits (ms scale) when token buckets indicate transient bursts and escalates to exponential backoff on repeated failures. This reduces tail-latency impact for multi-stream clients sharing a single Dedicated reservation.

Other ergonomics: improves Context propagation in the stream iterator/consumer so calling code can cancel from a single context and expect immediate tear-down across the handshake + reconnect path. We also tightened timeouts on the low-level dialer and exported a lightweight SetStreamOpts API for op-specific tuning.

Compatibility notes: All changes are opt-in. Default behavior remains the same unless callers opt into TridentSession or swap in the rate-aware policy via WithRetryPolicy(rateaware.New(...)). There is a minor public surface addition (types and functions) but no breaking signatures were changed.
